'''R4-G9''', also known as '''Geenine''', was a bronze-domed<ref name="CharEnc" /> [[R4-P astromech droid]] maintained by the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Like many Jedi R4-series droids, Geenine had an [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2 series]] dome, instead of the conical R4-series head.

==Biography==
[[File:R4-G9_Kenobi.png|thumb|left|250px|Kenobi orders R4-G9 back to ''Vigilance'' to report to Commander Cody]]
R4-G9 was originally assigned to [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]] to replace her previous astromech [[QT-KT/Legends|QT-KT]], who had been assigned elsewhere, and it operated aboard her blue-hued [[Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor/Legends|Eta-2 interceptor]]. During the search for [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]], Secura loaned the [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] to [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]. R4-G9 flew with Kenobi to pick up [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], before rendezvousing in the [[Karthakk system]]. Following the resolution of Obi-Wan's quest, he switched to a red-hulled interceptor, though apparently kept Secura's starfighter as a backup.

During the transition between the [[Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7 starfighter]] and its [[Delta-7B Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7B]] and Eta-2 successors, many astro-droids hard-wired into or truncated to fit Delta-7 starfighters had to be replaced by factory-model units. Such was the case with Obi-Wan Kenobi's [[R4-P17/Legends|R4-P17]], who was temporarily replaced by R4-G9 when Kenobi became one of the first Jedi to pilot the next-generation models. Obi-Wan requisitioned a direct link between the two droids to ensure all flight performance records could be transferred between them.

Kenobi was re-assigned R4-P17 when the droid was engineered to operate with the Delta-7B. After transferring to the Eta-2, R4 was destroyed onboard Obi-Wan's fighter during the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]]. She was replaced by G9 as Obi-Wan's droid co-pilot. G9 was stationed onboard [[Vigilance (Venator-class)/Legends|''Vigilance'']] following the resolution of the battle over [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].

When Obi-Wan was tasked with tracking down and eliminating [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], he flew with G9 to [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. There, he learned that the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]] had assumed control of [[Pau City/Legends|Pau City]], and ordered G9 to perform a diversionary tactic. G9 piloted the interceptor off the planet alone, returning to ''Vigilance'' while Obi-Wan remained on-world to locate Grievous.

==Behind the scenes==
In the non-canon video game "[[LEGO Star Wars]]," Geenine never made an appearance. Instead, in both the Game Boy Advance and console version of the game, it is, in fact, [[R4-P17]] who accompanies Obi-Wan to [[Utapau]]. This was most likely done to avoid confusion, as the game was primarily geared towards a younger audience.
